items.title: B627's residue: an expected type reaches a method's RECEIVER only where the method call itself has an expectation — `take(make().unwrap_or(5))` with `fun take(value: i32)` is still refused "cannot infer 'T'" (`let x: i32 = make().unwrap_or(5); take(x)` compiles)
items.body: B627 re-infers a receiver directed by `expected_types[method call]`, which an annotated binding, a typed tail or a decided parameter (B501) seeds. An argument at a NON-generic parameter records no expectation, so the chain has nothing to read. Rec: seed an argument call's expectation from a concrete parameter type too (the parameter is a typed position as surely as an annotation), measured on the estate (it moves `expected_types` for every argument call). Sizing S; the solver.

items.kind: native refusal of a JS-accepted program (S)
items.title: A generic struct literal no field grounds (`let both = Page { items = [], first = None };`) settled only by a LATER annotated binding (`let n: Page<i32> = both;`) runs on JS and is refused natively — "does not emit a value of an unbound generic type parameter (parameter 1 of struct `Page`) yet"; the same on v0.50.0
items.body: Met beside B628. The literal's binding settles as the declaration's `Page<T>` and the later annotation reconciles with it without reaching back; JS never needs the parameter, native does. Rec: the B580/residual sweep's question asked of the literal (a binding whose type keeps the struct's own parameter, read through a later typed binding, is refused with the annotation steer on both backends), or the later binding's type flows back to the literal's slot. Sizing S; the solver.

items.title: native-53's B636's in-place twin: a later argument WRITING the lent place in place — `log.items.push({ log.items.push(1); 9 })` — checks clean; JS prints 2 and rustc refuses the native emission (E0499: `log.items` borrowed mutably twice), reported as a backend defect
items.body: Spec §6.4 rule 4 reads it as an invalidating mutation under the live `&mut` view, as the re-bind is. solver-53's `check_lent_root_rebinds` refuses the re-bind only (its brief). Rec: the same check widened to an in-place write of the lent place or a place under it (`log.items.push(..)`, `log.items[0] = ..`, a `&mut` call over it), with the same settle-first steer; estate counted first (expected 0). A captured root stays F138's. Sizing S; the checks.

items.title: B627's refusal residue: a bare static whose bounded impl binder only its return carries, as the TAIL of an unannotated function (`fun tail_of() { Holder::build() }`), is still "internal: a call resolved to `Make`'s requirement `make`, which has no body" on JS
items.body: `undetermined_value_flows_on` follows the call's value into a binding, a consuming call, a field read or a discarded statement, and leaves every other position (a list element, a tuple, a tail) to whatever types it, because those are usually typed. An unannotated function's tail is typed by nothing. Rec: a tail of a function whose return type is inferred continues the walk at the function's call sites (or is refused there when the inferred return keeps the binder). Sizing XS-S; the checks.
